name: Pendjari National Park
subtitle: Pendjari National Park is a savanna reserve in north-west Benin that forms part of the W-Arly-Pendjari complex shared with Burkina Faso and Niger.

facts.label: Area (Mongabay 2018 figure)
facts.value: 2,755 km² (1,063 sq mi); this differs from African Parks' 4,800 km²

facts.label: Management
facts.value: African Parks and the Benin Government assumed management in 2017

facts.label: Transboundary complex
facts.value: Part of the W-Arly-Pendjari complex, straddling Benin, Burkina Faso and Niger

facts.label: Lions
facts.value: The WAP complex holds 90% of the largest population of West African lions

facts.label: Other wildlife
facts.value: Critically Endangered Northwest African cheetah, elephants, leopards, buffalo and more than 400 bird species

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: More than $23 million committed by National Geographic Society, Wyss Foundation, African Parks and the Government of Benin

facts.label: Threats
facts.value: Poaching, agricultural expansion at the periphery, rising livestock numbers, illegal logging and illegal fishing

facts.label: Population pressure
facts.value: Local human population growing around the park; poaching a problem

parts.text: Pendjari National Park is a savanna reserve in north-west Benin that forms part of the W-Arly-Pendjari complex shared with Burkina Faso and Niger. African Parks, with the Government of Benin, has managed it since 2017. Sources give its area as 4,800 km² (African Parks) or 2,755 km² (a 2018 Mongabay report), and name poaching, agricultural expansion and illegal logging as pressures.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.
